nodes.name: schema_v3.py
nodes.summary: Reader for the hybrid_gnn_lstm_v3 sample contract.
nodes.docstring_full:
Reader for the hybrid_gnn_lstm_v3 sample contract.

The v2 pipeline predicted one roof-displacement trace from a pooled graph
embedding, so it only ever read six arrays. v3 exports the full structural
response -- per-floor kinematics, per-element forces, per-hinge rotations,
per-joint forces -- which is what the per-node and per-element decoders need.

Two things about v3 drive the design here.

Sampling rate is not uniform. Floor kinematics, story drift and base shear are
recorded every step; element forces, joint forces and hinge rotations are
recorded every NTHA_ELEMENT_HISTORY_STRIDE (8) steps. The strided arrays ship
with an explicit index array (element_force_steps, hinge_rotation_steps)
giving the exact step each row was taken at, so a decoder running at full rate
can be supervised on the strided quantities by gathering those indices. No
resampling or assumed alignment is required, and none should be introduced.

Node and element counts vary per sample. Every per-node and per-element array
is therefore ragged across a batch and has to be concatenated with an index
vector, the way torch_geometric batches node features, rather than stacked.

nodes.summary: Fixed-design diagnostics on a saved record: a direction-explicit pushover, or one ground-motion pair with full-rate hinge loops.
nodes.docstring_full:
Fixed-design diagnostics on a saved record: a direction-explicit pushover, or one ground-motion pair with full-rate hinge loops.

    python Analysis/Fixed_Design_Diagnostics.py pushover --root D:/StructGNN_outputs/dv150_v10 --case case_0074         --runs y+ --output-root <folder> [--du 0.05 --max-steps 1200 --target-drift 0.04         --gravity-dead 1.0 --gravity-live 0.25 --pattern elf]

    python Analysis/Fixed_Design_Diagnostics.py ground-motion --root D:/StructGNN_outputs/dv150_v10 --case case_0074         --result-id 11 --set-name peer_strong_63 --scale 1.0 --output-root <isolated folder>         [--damping-ratio 0.05 --rayleigh-mode-i 0 --rayleigh-mode-j 2 --dt-factor 1.0 --x-only --plot-limit 24          --member-material IMKBilin]

Both commands read <root>/<case>/design.json and hash it, apply the record's
OWN geometry (record["geometry"]) and seismic site (record["seismic"]: the
named entry is applied, then SDS, SD1, S1 and R are checked value by value)
-- no generation plan is consulted -- and install the saved design
explicitly (Design_Driver.apply_design: sections, cage, hoops, slab,
transfer, slab reinforcement; no cache loading, no source-identity check,
no redesign). The saved record is read only and its hash is checked again at
the end. One worker, isolated output. Diagnostic evidence about the declared
model, kept apart from design qualification and training data.

pushover: Analysis.Pushover_Diagnostic.run_diagnostic for each requested run
in sequence, writing <output-root>/<case>/<run>/summary.json and steps.jsonl
plus a manifest with the record's SHA-256 and the current source identity.

ground-motion, in order: build the current IMK model with the production
NTHA conventions (Ground_Motion_Main.build_gravity_modal_state: elastic
reference modal analysis, D + L gravity at factor 1.0 through the saved slab
transfer, then the post-gravity modal diagnostic); measure the gravity
state; verify the installed sections, reinforcement, slab and hinge registry
against the record (per member, end and sign for the beam strengths);
attach a full-rate material recorder to every hinge spring in the domain;
load the record pair with its component ids; run Analysis.NTHA.run_ntha
with Rayleigh damping from the reference modes; save the production
outputs; read the recorders within the retained window; evaluate every
spring against its own installed backbone (path-aware and virgin-backbone
yield calls; native capping My/Kh + dp and the retained native du per sign,
Analysis/Hinge_Hysteresis_Diagnostic); justify a history stride against the full rate; plot the
yielded loops; write manifest.json. A failed or empty solve still writes the
manifest with the observed failure and no fabricated response.

Merged on 2026-09-25 from Design/Benchmark_Diagnostic.py (which used to take
the geometry and site from the generation plan; it now takes them from the
record like the ground-motion runner, as reviewed) and
Design/Pilot_Ground_Motion_Diagnostic.py (unchanged behaviour).

nodes.name: Hinge_Hysteresis_Diagnostic.py
nodes.summary: Full-rate hinge moment-rotation measurement for fixed-design diagnostics (2026-09-21).
nodes.docstring_full:
Full-rate hinge moment-rotation measurement for fixed-design diagnostics (2026-09-21). Production NTHA keeps hinge rotation histories at a stride and force ENVELOPES only, so a loop cannot be drawn from a generated run. This module attaches OpenSees element recorders to every IMK hinge spring before an analysis, reads them back afterwards, and evaluates each spring against the backbone actually installed on that hinge end and sign (Analysis.Pushover_Diagnostic.hinge_inventory reads Model.IMK_Hinges .hinge_registry). Nothing here redesigns, rebuilds a design record, or writes outside the caller's output directory. Measurement path ---------------- * One recorder per spring axis covers every hinge zero-length element: ``recorder Element -file

-time -precision 12 -ele material stressStrain``. Each row is [analysis time, (moment, rotation) per element in tag order]: the IMKBilin material's "stress" is the spring moment (kip-in) and its "strain" the spring rotation (rad), the conjugate pair of the spring in its own frame (probed 2026-09-21: identical to ``basicForce`` and ``deformation`` of the element at every step). Spring index 1 is the y' material (about global X for a column, vertical bending for a beam); index 2 the z' material (about global Y for a column, in-plane bending for a beam). Signs are the spring's: for a beam, hogging is POSITIVE rotation at end i and NEGATIVE at end j, and the installed positive / negative strengths follow (Model.IMK_Hinges._create_end_hinge). The element-end negation used by the pushover diagnostic's joint equilibrium is NOT applied here: a loop is plotted in the spring's own pair. * Rows are written at every committed analysis step, including the sub-steps of a recovery strategy (NTHA's subdivide fallback commits ten sub-steps for one record step), so histories are aligned by the time column, never by row index. * Yield is identified from the FULL-RATE history of each spring in two ways that are both reported. The path-aware call decomposes every step into an elastic part dM / Ke and a plastic part dtheta - dM / Ke and counts a step as plastic when its tangent is below half the installed Ke; accumulated positive and negative plastic rotation then say whether the spring yielded in each direction, INCLUDING yielding on the shifted (kinematic) branch after a reversal, where IMKBilin yields on the other side while the rotation is still on the first side and the moment is below that sign's Fy (review finding, 2026-09-21). The virgin-backbone call (peak rotation beyond Fy / Ke of that sign, peak moment reaching that sign's Fy, both from the extrema) is kept beside it, as is the production one-sided peak-based plastic rotation of Ground_Motion_Main._hinge_backbone_rows; disagreements are flagged. This path-aware decomposition is a legacy Bilin diagnostic, not a validated plastic-rotation measure for peak-oriented or pinched reloading. For those laws we report virgin-envelope exceedance and leave accumulated plastic rotation unavailable. Reversal yielding below that envelope can be missed. The energy figure is the signed work integral less the change in stored elastic energy on the initial Ke (net_work_minus_initial_ke_storage_kip_in; an exact discrete identity: zero for an elastic spring on any open path). It is NOT dissipated energy: once the stiffness deteriorates the recoverable part is no longer on Ke, and a partial cycle can leave it negative. * Capping and cutoff are read from each spring's OWN installed native points, per sign (Model/IMK_Spring_Mapping.spring_points and rotation_demand; frozen IMK V2 calibration, 2026-10-29): native yield My/Kh, native capping My/Kh + dp, and the retained native du, which is a provisional numerical cutoff, not a collapse rotation. The flat theta_p / theta_pc of the registry are MEMBER intervals (native dp/dpc differ from them under the frozen calibration) and are never compared with a spring rotation. A spring rotation is a local native rotation, not a story drift and not a member chord rotation.

nodes.name: Hinge_Moment_Rotation.py
nodes.summary: Synchronized hinge moment-rotation histories: the export schema of the V2 learning target (2026-10-01).
nodes.docstring_full:
Synchronized hinge moment-rotation histories: the export schema of the V2 learning target (2026-10-01).

Analysis.NTHA reads, at every scheduled snapshot, the relative rotation AND the conjugate moment of both
springs of every member hinge from the same committed state (zeroLength ``deformation`` and
``basicForce``; the pair the full-rate ``material i stressStrain`` recorder writes). This module turns
that result into files with an explicit schema, and compares it with recorder output on matched times.

Files written beside the other NTHA outputs:

  hinge_moment_rotation.npz          float64 arrays (see ARRAYS)
  hinge_moment_rotation_schema.json  what every array means, the sampling, the sign conventions, the
                                     reference state, the solver status, the identities, the limits
  hinge_springs.csv                  one row per spring (hinge element x local axis), in column order

What is stored and what is not:
  * rows are SCHEDULED SNAPSHOTS: one per stored scheduled step, after that step converged. When a step
    is recovered by subdivision OpenSees commits ten internal sub-steps; those are not snapshots and are
    not stored. ``commit_count`` says how many states the transient analysis had committed at each row,
    so a full-rate recorder (one row per commit) is matched by time or by commit count, never by a row
    number of this file;
  * values are ABSOLUTE and include the gravity-equilibrated state; that state is stored separately
    (``gravity_*``), so increments are a subtraction the reader makes knowingly;
  * a query that returned nothing is NaN and is counted; nothing is filled with zero;
  * a failed or truncated analysis writes what it has, with the status, and no fabricated rows.

The rotation is the TOTAL relative spring rotation of a member calibration that still contains
Haselton's bar-slip share wherever no face interface owns it (Model/Deformation_Ownership); it is not
experimentally isolated plastic flexure. Hinge histories alone do not establish a unique global
solution: floor motion, story drift and base shear are kept beside them as reference data.

hinge_moment_rotation_v2 (frozen IMK V2 calibration, 2026-10-29): the spring table states each installed
spring's member-to-native calibration. theta_p / theta_pc are the MEMBER Haselton intervals and theta_u the
retained native du; under the frozen calibration the installed native dp / dpc differ from the member
intervals, so the native points per sign (My/Kh, dp, dpc, My/Kh + dp, du), the half-member reference (K0, Kb,
My/K0, the member cap) and the energy anchor (energy reference yield rotation, lambda_H) are separate columns
(Model/IMK_Spring_Mapping.spring_points). A v1 table has none of them: its theta_p / theta_pc were the
installed native values only because the pre-freeze rule installed the member intervals directly.

nodes.name: Joint_Loops_Diagnostic.py
nodes.summary: Full-rate loops of the joint pinching springs in a fixed-design ground-motion diagnostic (2026-09-27).
nodes.docstring_full:
Full-rate loops of the joint pinching springs in a fixed-design ground-motion diagnostic (2026-09-27).

The production ground-motion outputs keep the joint springs' envelopes (``joint_springs.csv``) and a
coarse force array; this module adds, for the diagnostic only and behind ``--joint-loops``, what the
hinge diagnostic keeps for the member hinges: one text recorder per plane over every joint spring
element at the analysis rate, an evaluation row per spring against its installed law, the energy-ranked
loop gallery and a compressed history file. Nothing here is written by the generation scheduler, so a
dataset run stays as light as before.

Planes: the joint element is ``zeroLength ... -mat m4 m5 -dir 4 5`` (Model/Joint_Springs), so recorder
material index 1 is direction 4 (the y-z plane, the springs the y beams load, axis "y") and index 2 is
direction 5 (the x-z plane, axis "x").

nodes.name: NTHA.py
nodes.summary: Analysis/NTHA.py ================ Nonlinear Time-History Analysis (NLTHA) for the RC 3D MRF.
nodes.docstring_full:
Analysis/NTHA.py
================
Nonlinear Time-History Analysis (NLTHA) for the RC 3D MRF.

Design decisions
----------------
* Follows the same step-by-step convergence-recovery pattern as Pushover.py.
* Element force envelopes are tracked in-memory at every converged step
  using the same ``localForce`` query as Graph_Exporter, so the results are
  directly compatible with ``collect_element_end_force_rows()``.
* Rayleigh damping is applied with mass-proportional (a0) and
  initial-stiffness-proportional (a1) coefficients derived from two modal
  periods (default: modes 1 and 3, which for a symmetric 3D frame capture
  both translational directions).
* Gravity loads must already be applied before calling ``run_ntha()``.
  The function adds the ground motion pattern on top of the existing
  gravity state.

Return value
------------
dict with keys:
    status              convergence summary (see _make_status)
    time_history        list[float]  – time at each completed step (s)
    roof_disp_x         list[float]  – roof X-displacement history (in)
    roof_disp_y         list[float]  – roof Y-displacement history (in)
    peak_story_drift_x  list[float]  – per-story peak |drift ratio| in X
    peak_story_drift_y  list[float]  – per-story peak |drift ratio| in Y
    element_envelope    dict  {ele_tag: {'max': [12 floats], 'min': [12 floats]}}
    node_envelope       dict  {node_tag: {'max': [6 floats], 'min': [6 floats]}}
    record_summary_x    dict  – summarize_record() output for X ground motion
    record_summary_y    dict  – summarize_record() output for Y GM, or None
    damping_ratio       float
    rayleigh_a0         float  – mass coefficient
    rayleigh_a1         float  – initial-stiffness coefficient

Hinge histories (every ``hinge_history_stride``-th scheduled step; two values per hinge, local y then z,
in ``hinge_tag_order``), read together from the same committed state:
    hinge_rotation_history      list[rows][2H]  total relative spring rotation, rad
    hinge_moment_history        list[rows][2H]  conjugate spring moment, kip-in
    hinge_rotation_steps        list[rows]      0-based scheduled step of each row
    hinge_history_time          list[rows]      analysis time of each row, s
    hinge_history_strategy      list[rows]      how that scheduled step converged
    hinge_history_commit_count  list[rows]      states committed by the transient analysis up to the row
    hinge_gravity_state         dict            rotation and moment before the first transient step
    hinge_history_missing_values int            query values that came back empty (stored as NaN)
Rows are scheduled snapshots; the internal sub-steps of a subdivided recovery are never stored. Values
are absolute (they include the gravity state). Analysis/Hinge_Moment_Rotation writes them with a schema.
Floor accelerations are relative to the ground; story_drift_history holds unsigned drift ratios.

nodes.name: Pushover_Diagnostic.py
nodes.summary: Direction-explicit fixed-design pushover diagnostics (benchmark preparation, 2026-09-20).
nodes.docstring_full:
Direction-explicit fixed-design pushover diagnostics (benchmark preparation, 2026-09-20).

This is not the production pushover. ``Analysis/Pushover.py`` drives DOF 1
of the roof master under the uniform FX_FLOOR pattern of Loads/Lateral_Loads,
reads X reactions only and classifies hinges with Analysis/Mechanism_Checks
against each installed spring's native points per sign
(mechanism_diagnostics_v2); it has no Y or reverse-direction path. This module pushes the
roof master in +X, -X, +Y or -Y under an explicit, recorded lateral pattern
on top of a declared gravity state and records, at every converged step:

* the signed floor-master displacements (ux, uy, rz) and the signed edge
  displacements of the loaded direction;
* every column's local end forces, the internal moment about the loaded
  bending axis transformed to the joint faces, and the story shear it
  carries in the push direction (sign rule below);
* every beam's end forces and its vertical-bending end moments;
* every IMK hinge's deformation and moment with yield / native capping /
  native du cutoff events measured against the points of the spring
  actually installed on that end and axis, for the native sign of the
  rotation (Model.IMK_Spring_Mapping.spring_points); the du is a
  provisional numerical cutoff, not a collapse rotation;
* the base reactions, the applied lateral loads and the gravity state;
* the column-to-line story shear sums per frame line;
* equilibrium and sign checks: base shear, story shear per story, the
  moment balance at every joint for the lateral increment, and the
  linearity of every column's moment diagram, all reported as residuals.

Gravity and lateral responses are kept apart: the gravity state is step 0
and every later step also carries its increment from it. Nothing here
redesigns, rebuilds the design record or writes outside ``output_dir``.

Sign conventions (validated by tests/test_pushover_diagnostic.py on a
cantilever and on a small frame):

* Column elements use vecxz = (1, 0, 0) with local x upward: local y is
  -global Y and local z is +global X. ``localForce`` is the 12-vector
  [N, Vy, Vz, T, My, Mz] at end i (bottom) then end j (top), the forces
  acting ON the element at its ends. The story shear a column carries in
  +X is -Vz_i; in +Y it is +Vy_i.
* The internal moment along a column (no transverse load) is linear:
  M(x) = -My_i - Vz_i x for bending about local y (X push) and
  M(x) = -Mz_i + Vy_i x for bending about local z (Y push), x measured
  from end i; M(L) equals My_j (Mz_j), which is checked at every step.
* Beam elements use vecxz = (0, 0, 1): local z is +Z (up) and vertical
  bending is My with shear Vz, for beam_x (local y = +Y) and beam_y (local
  y = -X) alike.
* Global moments about the loaded bending axis at a joint: X push (about
  global Y): column -My, beam_x +My, beam_y torsion +T; Y push (about
  global X): column +Mz, beam_y -My, beam_x torsion +T. Their sum over the
  members at a joint is zero for the lateral increment.
* A hinge's moment is the physical element's end moment about the spring
  axis; its deformation is the spring's own.

nodes.name: Response_Spectrum.py
nodes.summary: Analysis/Response_Spectrum.py =============================
nodes.docstring_full:
Analysis/Response_Spectrum.py
=============================

Elastic response spectra for ground-motion records.

This file existed as an empty placeholder. The only implementation lived in
the surrogate package, where the generator could not reach it, so intensity
scaling had no way to ask how hard a record shakes a structure at its own
period. That is the question the whole calibration turns on: a record's PGA
says little about what it does to an eight-story frame.

Unit system: acceleration in in/sec^2, periods in seconds, spectral
acceleration returned in g.

nodes.summary: Reproducible PCA analysis of an exported RC parameter-space embedding.
nodes.docstring_full:
Reproducible PCA analysis of an exported RC parameter-space embedding.

Companion to ``RC Hybrid Surrogate Model/export_raw_embeddings.py``: reads the
``raw_vectors.tsv`` (+ sibling ``feature_names.txt`` / ``metadata.tsv``) that
script writes and reports what the TensorFlow Embedding Projector's PCA view
never exposes on its own -- explained variance, per-component loadings named
back to real feature columns, a target-leakage smoke test, and an optional
static scatter figure -- all reproducible from files already in the repo
instead of a browser session's memory.

Pass ``--features`` pointing at the RAW (unstandardized) export
(``raw_vectors.tsv``), not the pre-standardized ``vectors.tsv`` that gets
uploaded to the Projector: this script does its own standardization by
default so ``--no-standardize`` can meaningfully compare against it. Feeding
it an already-standardized file makes ``--no-standardize`` a no-op.

Example usage:

    python Analyze_Parameter_Space.py \
        --features ".../structure_record/raw_vectors.tsv" --top-loadings 8

    python Analyze_Parameter_Space.py \
        --features ".../structure_record/raw_vectors.tsv" \
        --no-standardize --top-loadings 8

    python Analyze_Parameter_Space.py \
        --features ".../structure_record/raw_vectors.tsv" \
        --color-by num_floor --color-by peak_drift_percent \
        --figure pca_projection.png

nodes.summary: Freeze an explicitly scoped, portable weighted-intensity diagnostic plan.
nodes.docstring_full:
Freeze an explicitly scoped, portable weighted-intensity diagnostic plan.

Plan construction and preflight never build a structural model or run NTHA.
Input design roots and output root must be inside RC Structure, copied with the
same relative layout on each device. One master plan assigns disjoint jobs to
1--4 devices. Each device runs Run_Weighted_Seismic_Calibration.py --shard N.

Scales are RAW common X/Y acceleration multipliers, not spectral alpha. A
passing weighted score does not close M1, qualify hinges, or release training.
The default refuses all unqualified designs. --allow-open-m1-diagnostic permits
only the single existing M1 check to remain open and preserves that fact.

nodes.name: Calibrate_Intensity.py
nodes.summary: Data_Generation/Calibrate_Intensity.py ======================================
nodes.docstring_full:
Data_Generation/Calibrate_Intensity.py
======================================

Turn a pilot batch into an intensity rule that produces a target drift
distribution.

Why a rule rather than a ladder
-------------------------------
A uniform set of scale factors applied to every record wastes most of the
compute. The drift a record produces depends on how hard it shakes a
structure at that structure's own period, and that varies by roughly an order
of magnitude across a dataset spanning four to nine stories and five hazard
levels. A uniform ladder therefore leaves short stiff frames elastic while
driving tall flexible ones to collapse, and the resulting drift distribution
is whatever falls out rather than what was wanted.

This module fits the relationship on a pilot batch and inverts it: given a
target drift, it returns the scale factor that should produce it.

The model
---------
    log(drift) = a + b log(SaGM(T1)) + c log(T1)

fitted by least squares on completed pilot runs. b near one is the
equal-displacement rule; letting it float lets the data disagree. The T1 term
absorbs the systematic difference between short and tall frames that remains
after normalizing by spectral demand.

Inverting for a target drift:

    log(Sa_required) = (log(target) - a - c log(T1)) / b
    scale_factor     = Sa_required / SaGM_unscaled(T1)

Scheduler constraint
--------------------
The scheduler must not import OpenSees, so it cannot compute T1 or a response
spectrum when it builds a plan. The calibration artifact therefore carries
everything needed to derive a scale factor from geometry alone: the fitted
coefficients, an empirical T1/Ta ratio so the period can be estimated from
the ASCE approximate formula, and the precomputed spectrum of every eligible
record pair.

Usage
-----
    python Calibrate_Intensity.py --dataset-root <pilot root> \
        --output intensity_calibration.json

nodes.name: Check_Dataset_DCR.py
nodes.summary: Screen a generated dataset for ACI 318-19 demand-capacity ratios > 1.
nodes.docstring_full:
Screen a generated dataset for ACI 318-19 demand-capacity ratios > 1.

The batch generation pipeline never runs a design check (see Redesign.py,
which is only wired into Main.py), so nothing in a generated dataset records
whether the fixed sections were actually adequate for the demand each
geometry/record pairing produced. This screens that after the fact.

Reuses RC_Design_Check.py's own ACI 318-19 formulas -- same P-M interaction
diagram, same shear and flexure equations -- applied to the per-element
force envelope (element_end_force_envelope.csv) that every completed NTHA run
already stores. No OpenSees model rebuild required.

Methodology note: the envelope stores max/min per force component
independently, not concurrent (P, M, V) triples at a single instant. The
column P-M check therefore brackets conservatively, evaluating both the max
and min axial force against the envelope moment and taking the worse case.
That makes this a screening tool, not a certified concurrent code check.

Usage
-----
    python Check_Dataset_DCR.py --dataset-root "<root>" [--dataset-root "<root2>"]
    python Check_Dataset_DCR.py --dataset-root "<root>" --csv dcr_by_case.csv

nodes.name: Generate_Hybrid_Dataset.py
nodes.summary: Data_Generation/Generate_Hybrid_Dataset.py ==========================================
nodes.docstring_full:
Data_Generation/Generate_Hybrid_Dataset.py
==========================================

Automation entrypoint for RC Structure hybrid GNN + LSTM data generation.

Two modes are supported:
  1. Compile existing NTHA result folders into hybrid_sample.npz files.
  2. Optionally run Ground_Motion_Main.py first, then compile the new outputs.

Examples
--------
Compile existing successful NTHA outputs:
    python -B Data_Generation/Generate_Hybrid_Dataset.py --compile-existing

Run PEER result IDs 1 and 2, then compile:
    python -B Data_Generation/Generate_Hybrid_Dataset.py --run-ntha --result-id 1 --result-id 2

Run the first 5 pairs from the manifest, then compile:
    python -B Data_Generation/Generate_Hybrid_Dataset.py --run-ntha --limit 5

Stop a running batch safely from another terminal:
    python -B Data_Generation/Generate_Hybrid_Dataset.py --request-stop

The same generation command can then be run again. Successful NTHAs and
compiled samples are reused, while an interrupted active case is retried.

nodes.name: Record_Hinge_Hysteresis.py
nodes.summary: Re-run one generated case with recorders on its IMK hinges, and plot the moment-rotation hysteresis.
nodes.docstring_full:
Re-run one generated case with recorders on its IMK hinges, and plot the
moment-rotation hysteresis.

Generated NTHA output only stores force/rotation ENVELOPES, never the full
moment-rotation history, so proving the IMK hinge model behaves correctly
(elastic slope matches the spring stiffness Kh, yield at My, capping at
Mc = FmaxFy*My reached at the native rotation My/Kh + dp, post-capping
degradation) requires re-running the case with element recorders attached.

This rebuilds the model exactly the way Ground_Motion_Main.py does
(build_gravity_modal_state() then run_ntha()) so the model is identical to
the one that produced the dataset, attaches recorders to the requested
hinges, runs the analysis, and plots the result.

Every loop is drawn against its OWN installed spring, read from the hinge
registry of the rebuilt model per member end, bending axis and native sign
(Model/IMK_Spring_Mapping.spring_points): native yield My/Kh, native capping
My/Kh + dp and, under the frozen IMK V2 calibration (2026-10-29), the
member-reference yield My/K0 for comparison. The plotted rotation is the native
zeroLength spring rotation in milliradians: not a story drift and not a member
chord rotation. The native du is a provisional numerical cutoff, not a collapse
rotation. The rerun installs the CURRENT member spring calibration; a case
generated under another one is reported, never silently mixed.

Important: hinges only exist where Structure_Parameters enables them.
With IMK_APPLY_TO_COLUMNS = False, column elements have no hinge at all and
their recorders will produce a file containing only a time column -- point
this at beam elements in that configuration.

Usage
-----
    python Record_Hinge_Hysteresis.py \
        --case-dir "<root>/cases/case_3331" --set-name peer_expansion_30k \
        --element 266 --element 262

Geometry and result_id are read from the case's own automation_summary.json,
so the rerun matches the original generation run.

The weighted objective is separate from the existing is_inelastic label.

    python Data_Generation/Run_Weighted_Seismic_Calibration.py --plan plan.json --shard 1

nodes.name: Seismic_Response_Score.py
nodes.summary: Pure response scoring for seismic intensity calibration.
nodes.docstring_full:
Pure response scoring for seismic intensity calibration.

The drift and hinge values are references, not individual acceptance gates or
upper limits. Ratios are deliberately uncapped: excess response in one metric
can compensate for another below its reference. Consequently this score does
not require all four references to be attained and a sufficiently large single
metric can dominate it. Raw components remain visible for diagnostic review.

This objective does not establish analysis completion, design qualification,
training eligibility, cycle counts, frequency coverage, or yielding at every
story. Those checks belong to the caller. It does not replace ``is_inelastic``.
No OpenSees or numerical-analysis dependencies are needed to evaluate it.

nodes.name: Code_Check_Contract.py
nodes.summary: The authoritative code-check result of one grouped design candidate and the contract its evaluation must meet (code-check audit of the genetic search, 2026-10-30).
nodes.docstring_full:
The authoritative code-check result of one grouped design candidate and the contract its evaluation must meet
(code-check audit of the genetic search, 2026-10-30).

Three results are kept apart and none stands in for another:

  preliminary screen   Grouped_Design's ``candidate_screen_passed``: no recorded failure in the families it reads
                       and a settled reinforcement pass. It names no failure; it is not evidence that a check passed.
  code check           this module: every check the final design requires, derived from that design's own topology
                       and system assignment (never from the list under review), present exactly once, well formed,
                       and passing. Known failures stay visible beside unknown checks; an unknown check is neither a
                       failure nor a pass. Review-dependent items (engineering assessments the code does not make) are
                       listed apart: they neither fail nor pass the computed checks and are never asserted here.
  qualification        Design.Grouped_Record.qualify_grouped_design on the saved record (integrity, recomputation and
                       the reviews), the gate before any time-history analysis. GENERATION_RELEASE_READY is untouched.

The candidate scope (SCOPE) is the ACI 318-19 special-moment-frame strength and detailing checks the evaluator
implements, with the supporting ASCE 7-22 drift, stability, vertical-regularity and torsional-amplification checks;
its exclusions are named. Nonlinear response is not part of it: its status is reported as not requested, never as
a failed code check.

``expected_inventory`` reads only the realized design (member groups, joints, systems, story count) and the
declared configuration. ``code_check_result`` classifies the supplied rows against it. ``assess_evaluation`` is the
boundary a search applies to an evaluation record before ranking or archiving it: schema, completion flags,
identities, the binding of the rows to the final design, and an independent recomputation of the result.

Contract v2 (2026-11-01 closure review): a proven reinforcement cycle resolved on verification
(Grouped_Design.resolve_cycle: the adopted state meets the selection's own rules, its hoops are a fixed point and its
capacity design is accepted) completes reinforcement_settled and longitudinal_selection_settled for that final state
only (numerical_completion). Both flags stay false in the record, so no convergence is claimed; every other flag, and
the code check itself, is unchanged.

nodes.name: Concrete_Grades.py
nodes.summary: Concrete grades by structural role in the grouped design engine (2026-10-23).
nodes.docstring_full:
Concrete grades by structural role in the grouped design engine (2026-10-23).

A grade family is a set of member groups that hold one specified concrete strength (f'c) over every story band. The
search moves a family one rung of its own ladder at a time (Design.Grouped_Search), and only for a failure of one of
its own groups:

  band policy (every frame is part of the seismic force-resisting system, SFRS)
      column            Section_Design.COLUMN_CONCRETE_STRENGTHS_KSI, from the seed's column grade (as before)
      beam              Section_Design.BEAM_CONCRETE_STRENGTHS_KSI, from the seed's beam grade (as before)
  two-system policies (perimeter frames, and the core ring or core lines the layout ladder adds)
      sfrs_column       the special moment frame column ladder (6-10 ksi), from the seed's column grade
      gravity_column    Section_Design.GRAVITY_COLUMN_CONCRETE_STRENGTHS_KSI (5, 6, 7 ksi), from 5 ksi, never above 7
      beam              every beam, special-frame and gravity, on the special moment frame beam ladder (5, 6, 8 ksi),
                        from the seed's beam grade

The gravity ladder is the user decision DEC-SFV6-GRAVITY-CONCRETE-20261023. The system of a group is the one its
grouping policy assigns from the active layout (Model.Member_Groups): a column the core ring or the core lines bring
into the SFRS is an sfrs_column under that policy and starts from the special-frame seed grade. A family is one grade
over the full height, so a column line keeps one grade (Design.SMRF_Transitions requires that at band boundaries).

Gravity beams keep the shared beam grade for now. The same decision gives them the 5-7 ksi ladder, but the floor model
casts the slab with the beams: the one beam grade of a floor is the slab's grade (Design.SMRF_Floor_Sections,
Design.SMRF_Slab), and each T or L flange takes its own web's concrete (Model.Member_Properties,
Design.SMRF_Beam_Slab_Strength). Every floor carries special-frame beams on its perimeter beside gravity beams inside,
so two beam grades on one floor need a declared slab grade, pour boundary and flange-concrete rule. That rule is not
decided; until it is, ``SEPARATE_GRAVITY_BEAMS`` stays False and a record states whether the shared beam grade lies
on the gravity ladder (``gravity_beams`` in ``describe``).

Joint concrete is unchanged: joint shear and hook development use the f'c of the column below the joint at every
joint (Model.Member_Properties.JOINT_CORE_CONVENTION), and column-strength concrete is declared placed in the floor at
the column where the column's f'c exceeds 1.4 times the floor's (ACI 318-19 15.5(a), user decision 2026-10-03). A
gravity column frames only gravity beams in every layout, and 7 ksi is 1.4 times a 5 ksi floor.

Records written before this module carry no ``concrete_grade_policy``; they are read under the earlier rule, one
grade per member type (``LEGACY_POLICY_ID``).

Design/Config.py
Configuration dataclasses for the RC frame design pipeline.

Usage

nodes.name: Design_Driver.py
nodes.summary: Design/Design_Driver.py =======================
nodes.docstring_full:
Design/Design_Driver.py
=======================

Searches for a frame design candidate and writes traceable SMRF qualification
evidence. This is NOT a complete building-code design or certification.

Why this exists
---------------
Redesign.run_iterative_redesign resizes longitudinal bars against a
gravity-only demand, and it was only ever wired into Main.py. The dataset
generator calls Ground_Motion_Main, which had no design step at all, so every
generated structure kept the Structure_Parameters defaults regardless of its
height or span. This driver closes both gaps:

  * demand comes from the ASCE 7-22 seismic combination (1.2D + 0.5L + E),
    not gravity alone, so member sizes respond to building height
  * the search covers section dimensions and concrete strength as well as
    reinforcement, via the ladders in Design/Section_Design.py

Design depends only on geometry and loads, never on the ground motion, so the
result is cached per structure and reused by every record and intensity run of
that case. Building it once instead of once per analysis is the difference
between designing a thousand structures and designing several thousand.

Unit system: kip, inch, ksi.

nodes.name: Design_Evidence_Profile.py
nodes.summary: Per-run design-evidence profile: the explicit, validated slab evidence configuration of one run (2026-11-01).
nodes.docstring_full:
Per-run design-evidence profile: the explicit, validated slab evidence configuration of one run (2026-11-01).

The default run computes single-mesh slab actions and asserts nothing: no slab layout is selected and the strong-column
checks that need the developed slab stay unknown. A profile changes that only by what it declares, in one JSON file:

  slab_refinement          the numerical mesh refinement plan of the slab actions
                           (Design.SMRF_Slab_Refinement: an explicit mesh plan or a named recipe), loaded apart from
                           the assertions, so numerical evidence can be produced while every assertion stays false. Its
                           tolerance is the declared investigation criterion (``slab_refinement_basis``), not an ACI
                           requirement or a validated error bound.
  slab_action_assertions   the engineering assertions (Design.Config.SlabActionAssertions), every field explicit. A true
                           flag needs a reviewed profile: review_status "reviewed_for_declared_scope", the review block
                           (who, when, on what basis, the decision and the evidence files with their sha256, checked on
                           load), the assertion provenance equal to that review (never filled in here), a refinement
                           plan, and the floor section sets the review covers.
  scope                    the case (id, and the sha256 of the run's --case-file, or of its --manifest file for a
                           manifest run), the analysis profile, the geometry, the slab materials and
                           loads and the slab policy (live load patterning, transfer mesh, thickness ladder) the profile
                           covers, checked against the run before any evaluation; and, for assertions, the floor
                           section signatures (Design.SMRF_Floor_Sections) and the slab thickness reviewed (one
                           thickness of the declared ladder). A candidate
                           with a floor outside them, or another slab thickness, is evaluated unasserted
                           (FloorAnalysisConfig.slab_assertion_floor_sections, slab_assertion_thickness_in).
  provenance, kind,        who prepared the file, when and why; ``kind`` "unreviewed_example", "test_fixture" (loaded
  review_status            only where a caller allows it: the runner refuses it) or "reviewed"; the review status.

Rejected on load: unknown, missing or repeated keys at every level, a boolean given as anything but a JSON boolean,
blank or undated provenance, a malformed plan (key sets, tolerances, the recipe name, its levels and shell budget, an
explicit plan's meshes), an asserted flag without a matching review, a reviewed thickness off the declared ladder, a
review whose evidence files are missing or differ from their recorded hash, a PROBE stamp in the assertions or in any
review block outside a test fixture. A scope that differs from the run is refused by the runner, which also resolves the
plan on the seed's floors before any evaluation.
Nothing is inherited from the PROBE configuration (Design.Verify_Designs.probe_config) and no approver is synthesized.

The profile enters the run before any evaluation: apply() returns the DesignConfig it implies (its slab_actions and
floor_analysis are in the evaluation identity), and summary() is the block the run's request carries (the generation
basis carries its id, kind, review status, asserted flag and ``identity_sha256``, which covers every field and the
hashes of the referenced evidence), so a changed plan, assertion,
review or scope is another identity and invalidates the cache and any checkpoint made under the old one. Nothing here
verifies anything: a reviewed profile records a decision taken elsewhere, for the scope it names.

nodes.name: Design_Figures.py
nodes.summary: Figures of one uniform design record: the structure in 3D, the member cross sections with their reinforcement, and the joint detailing with the joint shear table (verification stage ``figures``, 2026-10-02).
nodes.docstring_full:
Figures of one uniform design record: the structure in 3D, the member cross sections with their reinforcement,
and the joint detailing with the joint shear table (verification stage ``figures``, 2026-10-02).

Everything is read from the saved record (sections, reinforcement, the capacity-design cages, joints, anchorage and
splices, the slab layout, the detailing zones). Nothing is recomputed and no model is built. A value the record does
not carry is left out of the drawing and named in ``notes``; the stage never fails a case over a missing label. A
grouped record (``design_mode`` "grouped") is not drawn here: its members differ by group and the figures of the
grouped design are a later extension.

    draw_design_figures(record, out_dir, label="case_0001") -> {"files": [...], "notes": [...]}

nodes.name: Genetic_Diagnostics.py
nodes.summary: Normalized mutation diagnostics of one evaluated grouped design (genetic search, 2026-10-30).
nodes.docstring_full:
Normalized mutation diagnostics of one evaluated grouped design (genetic search, 2026-10-30).

The six mutation operators (Design.Genetic_Operators) read failures through this adapter only. It runs once per
evaluation, while the evaluator's in-memory record is still at hand, and keeps what routing needs:

  context      the parent the diagnostics belong to: its realized identity (cages and slab included), the run's
               evaluation basis, the declared genes and the parent's alleles, every group's physical description,
               and the joint topology the record's own strong-column and joint evidence was computed on.
  diagnostics  one entry per failed check row of a mapped source (and per failed strength component), with the
               original family / id / location, the declared comparison and units, the demand and capacity, the
               physical target (group, joint or joint type, axis, sway sign, story) and the dependencies its operator
               needs, each derived from the bound record (rows, completion flags, capacity and strength evidence).
  unknown      the rows that were not evaluated, grouped by check and reason code: evidence to obtain, never a
               reason to strengthen.

Nothing is trusted that the contract assessment (Design.Code_Check_Contract.assess_evaluation) did not validate:
an invalid record yields no diagnostics. A dependency is True only when the record shows it; a missing or malformed
item makes it False, and the router then abstains. No flag is set to obtain a proposal, nothing here is synthetic,
and a diagnostic grants no acceptance. Failures without a mapped source (and the analysis-shear component of a
strength row) are kept as unsupported diagnostics: they are reported, and the router abstains on them.

v2 (2026-10-30 review): a beam strength shortfall of a lane-limited group (the cages that reach the demand do not
thread the column, Group_Selection) is a bar-room deficit (beam_lane_limited_strength, H3), not a strength deficit;
the gravity column capacity-shear row is mapped; capacity-shear transverse selection needs the hoop selection to
have settled with a recorded outcome (an exhausted hoop ladder is an outcome); a column capacity-shear diagnostic
records whether the selected cage is the lightest the section admits (its ratio set by the minimum, not demand).

v3 (2026-10-30 second review): the gravity column capacity-shear row is authenticated against the producer's
per-direction record (a row that compares one direction's Ve with another direction's phi Vn is invalid evidence
for routing); a cage lighter than every admissible cage leaves the ratio-floor flag unknown; a lane-limited
shortfall's column levers come from the joint topology and follow its consistency (the record's topology_problems).

v4 (2026-10-30 fourth review round): the ratio-floor flag is read only on a settled longitudinal selection whose Ve
the probable-moment mechanism sets (not the analysis shear); an unevaluated gravity column capacity-shear row of a
column without selected hoops carries the reason the producer's own record shows (hoops_not_selected) instead of none.

v5 (2026-10-31 fifth review round): the mechanism test of the ratio-floor flag also requires the column-own Ve
method on the governing entry (the only method the grouped route builds; under another method the beams can set Ve
below the column's own envelope); hoops_not_selected is given only when the governing Ve is known, so the missing
hoops alone explain the unevaluated row.

v6 (2026-10-31 lower-perimeter cage audit): a beam flexural shortfall whose strength threading constrains (a stronger
admissible cage does not thread the column cages and the strongest threading cage still falls short; the selection's
threading evidence, Group_Selection) is beam_threading_constrained_strength (H3): the beam's own levers and the cores
that block the stronger cage, with the selection's geometry-only look-ahead of the core size. It is authenticated against
the record (constraints.beam_threading_evidence) and the group's final cage; without that the router abstains. A
lane-limited shortfall keeps its own meaning and route; an unlisted one stays a strength deficit (H2).

v7 (2026-10-31 cage-coordination review): the threading evidence keeps a core cage's own blockage apart from a column
transition's (a band-boundary joint whose bar inventory blocks the stronger cage, named by both column groups). A core
size target is read only from a look-ahead entry of scope core_cage; a transition's targets only from an entry of scope
transition_joint, for the band it resizes (the column above or the core below) at that joint's own inventory. An entry
without a scope gives no target. The cores whose own cage blocks are carried as blocking_core_cages.

v8 (2026-10-31 follow-up review): the same attribution reaches the other two triggers. A failed beam.bars_thread_column row
(beam_threading) states from its own lanes whether the core cage blocks (core_cage_blocks) and whether the transition
to the column above does (transition_blocks, with column_above_group checked against the joint topology); the
installed-cage lane evidence (constraints.beam_lane_evidence: this state's identity, the group's final cage) adds the
look-ahead targets of that joint, without a flexural shortfall. A lane-limited shortfall carries the selection's
threading fields when they authenticate. The router then grows a core only where its own cage blocks.

nodes.name: Genetic_Generation.py
nodes.summary: Bounded serial generation controller of the genetic search (SeisFrame GA v3, 2026-10-30).
nodes.docstring_full:
Bounded serial generation controller of the genetic search (SeisFrame GA v3, 2026-10-30).

One case, one grouping, one longitudinal steel grade and one evaluation basis per run. Every distinct child is
evaluated completely by the existing grouped evaluator (Grouped_Design.evaluate_candidate) and assessed by the
code-check contract (Code_Check_Contract.assess_evaluation) before it is ranked or archived. Evaluation is serial.

  initialization   the seed, then the declared initialization policy (INITIALIZATION_POLICIES).
  generations      parents drawn uniformly from the working population; per child, with the declared probability a
                   guided operator (H1-H5, Genetic_Operators.choose_guided) on the parent's own diagnostics, otherwise
                   (or when every diagnostic abstains) R1. No crossover, no adaptive weights. Repair, no-op and
                   duplicate filtering come before any evaluation; an input already evaluated is a cache hit.
  selection        Genetic_Population.select over the population and the generation's offspring (mu + lambda), every
                   child included (a stopped or raised one is listed in the queues, never a parent), with the
                   quarantine computed over the whole history. A stop between steps first selects what was evaluated
                   since the last selection. Progress is a new realized design (one no earlier observation of the run
                   realized), evaluated in the generation, that enters the population and either dominates a member
                   of the previous population (a better tier, more coverage under the same inventory, or better
                   progress measures under the same comparison signature; each member compared on its own record, one
                   quarantined in this selection not at all) or enters while that population, less its members
                   quarantined in this selection, had a free slot; or a code-accepted identity added to the registry.
                   Any other entry is not progress: by the diversity tie-break (a noncomparable design; the seeded
                   anchor is redrawn each generation) or by rank (a nondominated design that dominates no member).
                   Progress is measured against the previous population, not against every earlier parent. A
                   selection that ends underfilled keeps every eligible candidate, and the population never shrinks
                   except by quarantine, so free-slot entries reset the stagnation counter at most population_size
                   times plus once per quarantined member. A generation without a new evaluation
                   stops the search; a generation drawn while no parent existed (exploration) fills free slots, so
                   its entrants reset the counter, bounded by the exploration budget.
  outputs          an append-only observation history, a proposal log, generation records, per-evaluation artifacts,
                   and views recomputed from the whole history: accepted registry, diversity view, evidence queue,
                   analysis-recovery queue, unroutable failures, quarantine.

Two identities are kept apart: ``input_identity`` (the evaluation basis plus the complete submitted design, seed
cages included: the cache key) and ``realized_identity`` (the final design with its selected cages and slab: the
registry key). Every step is checkpointed with the random-generator state; a run resumes only under the same
configuration fingerprint, and one process at a time owns the run directory: an OS lease under which every run file
is written, the request a new run claims the directory with and the error record included. A controller runs once;
it is spent when its run returns or raises, and a new one continues the run. Solve counts are work
accounting: the evaluator's floor caches live in the process, so a resumed run may count more solves than an
uninterrupted one. A budget, time or bound stop is never a statement of structural infeasibility, and a code-accepted
design is not a qualified design: qualification (Grouped_Record) and nonlinear analysis stay separate.

v3_6 (2026-10-31): two declared proposal policies, part of the evaluation basis (proposal_policy) and so of every
binding to it (diagnostics, the input cache, the registry, the fingerprint): the guided selection
(GenerationConfig.guided_selection: uniform_operator_v1, the earlier rule, or severity_weighted_v1,
Genetic_Operators.choose_guided) and the beam-flexure steps (beam_jump_policy: local_frontier_v1, the earlier rule, or
demand_sized_v1). Under demand_sized_v1 each valid evaluation is screened while the evaluator's record is at hand, for
demand-sized farther options of its beam flexural shortfalls (Design.Genetic_Jumps), within a per-gene and
per-observation budget and the run's remaining wall time; the screen's time is the run's. The screen is kept with the
observation's diagnostics, ranks proposals and never certifies one. The guided probability, parent selection,
survival and acceptance are unchanged. A run's configured practical beam steel ratio ceiling is never above
Design.Config.BEAM_PRACTICAL_RATIO_AUTHORIZED_MAX.

v3_7 (2026-11-01): the selection policy severity_preferred_jumps_v1 (Genetic_Operators v10) gives preferred_share of the
guided draws to the parent's severe screened demand-sized proposals (failures at preferred_severe_utilization and
above) when there are any; it needs the demand_sized_v1 jumps, a positive beam_jump_min_gain and a preferred_share
below 1. A pool candidate drawn for a parent, in either branch, is kept in the checkpoint (preferred_drawn) and not
drawn from the preferred branch again. The counters (preferred_selection) keep apart what was proposed (eligible pool
candidates when a parent is first routed), drawn (by branch), completely evaluated, evaluated incompletely or with an
error, and accepted.

nodes.name: Genetic_Jumps.py
nodes.summary: Demand-sized beam-flexure jumps of the genetic search (2026-10-31): an analysis-free screen, on the evaluated parent's frozen member demands, of the farther legal catalog options of the beam levers a flexural shortfall's route offers.
nodes.docstring_full:
Demand-sized beam-flexure jumps of the genetic search (2026-10-31): an analysis-free screen, on the evaluated parent's
frozen member demands, of the farther legal catalog options of the beam levers a flexural shortfall's route offers.

Trigger. An authenticated beam flexural shortfall: a failed member.strength component routed as beam_flexure,
beam_lane_limited_strength or beam_threading_constrained_strength (Design.Genetic_Diagnostics), bound to the parent and
the run's basis, its dependencies shown, and its pair finite and positive: the governing member moment Mu against that
member's own phi Mn, per sign. The route already offers the beam's depth and width (and, except lane-limited, the beam
concrete family's grade) one local catalog step away (Genetic_Operators.frontier, the next grade). The screen adds at
most one farther option sized on the deficit per size gene (proposed under whichever of depth and width contains it)
and one per concrete family (grade_up).

Requirement. With the parent's demand frozen, for each failed component

    required capacity       = Mu / target DCR         (kip-in; GenerationConfig.beam_jump_target_dcr)
    capacity ratio required = (Mu / phi Mn) / target DCR

so a component at Mu / phi Mn = 1.728 with a target of 0.85 needs about 2.03 times its phi Mn. It is a capacity
requirement, never a multiplier of the beam's dimensions or steel: whether an option reaches it is priced.

Pricing (price_unit). The beam unit (the groups of the size tie, one shared cage) is priced as the selection prices it
(Group_Selection.select_beam_groups: evaluate_beam_candidate per group on the member-paired frozen demands, merged over
the tie) in the parent's realized design, every other group's cage frozen: the bar rows and effective depths the layering
gives the cage beside the crossing beams and column cages, the composite T/L strength of the final check, the clear
spacing, layer cap, threading, row depth, strength balance and minimum steel, and the face ratio limit
min(18.6.3.1, RebarConfig.rho_beam_practical_max) per face on the actual rows' effective depth (the run's DesignConfig;
nothing here assumes a ratio). An option's estimate is the selection pool's best cage: the strongest cage that threads
the frozen column cages when any does, otherwise the strongest admissible one. Cages are tried from the most steel down;
while a threading cage is sought, a cage that its bar size's lanes (from the layering) cannot thread is deferred, and
once one is admissible the scan stops below STEEL_SCAN_FRACTION of its steel. On the 34 sections screened for o0005 of
the 10-minute run (2026-10-31) the estimate equalled the full selection's best threading cage exactly, at about a tenth
of its time.

Options. A farther option is a catalog option of the gene in a lever's direction (depth: deeper and no narrower; width:
wider and no shallower; grade: a higher grade of the family's ladder) whose requested genome the profile repair keeps
(Genetic_Search.DesignSpace.repair: lower bands grow under an upper-band option, an induced change the proposal records).
It is priced after that same repair (Grouped_Search.enforce_banded_section_order). The parent's own section is priced
first and must reproduce the recorded utilization within BASELINE_TOLERANCE, or the gene's screen gives no target
(calibration_mismatch). Then the farthest option. If it reaches the target, the search narrows toward the smallest option
that does: bisection on the catalog order between the parent and the smallest option known to reach it, then the
options below that one not yet priced, nearest first (the estimates need not rise with the catalog order); the result
states whether every smaller option was priced (smallest_confirmed). If the farthest option does not reach the target,
the others from the farthest down. Bounded by GenerationConfig.beam_jump_max_sections pricings per gene (a grade option
costs one per beam unit it prices) and beam_jump_max_seconds per observation (and the run's remaining wall time); an
option the budget left unpriced is listed as unscreened, never as infeasible.

Shortlist. Per gene: the smallest priced option estimated to reach the target (catalog order: the flexural proxy b h^2,
or the grade ladder); when none is, the first priced option in catalog order within beam_jump_partial_tolerance of the
best estimate that improves on the parent and on every other local step priced by at least beam_jump_min_gain (a useful
partial improvement, outcome target_unmet_estimated: the end of the catalog is never called adequate because the
catalog ends). The pool of the estimate (threading, or admissible when no cage threads the frozen column cages) is kept
with it. The local steps stay proposals; an option equal to one only adds its estimate to that step's attribution.

Units. Every shortlisted option carries the estimate of each beam unit it prices (``units``) and every gene screen the
parent's own estimate of each unit (``unit_baselines``; a concrete family's from its units' size screens), so the
improvement a diagnostic is credited with is always its own unit's estimate against the same unit's baseline: a family
grade option's gene-level estimate is its worst unit's, which may be another band than the diagnostic's (v2,
2026-11-01). For the same reason every gene screen gives, per unit, the smallest priced option whose estimate for that
unit reaches the target with a cage that threads the frozen column cages (``unit_targets``: the option, the unit's
estimate, the option's gene-level estimate and pool, and smallest_confirmed: that unit was priced at every smaller legal
option, in a row the screen kept; a pricing the deadline cut confirms nothing for any unit of its row, as for the gene):
a smaller grade may bring one band to the target while the family's worst band needs more.

Not authoritative. The demand is frozen: a larger beam is stiffer and heavier, and the reanalysis redistributes demand;
the column cages are frozen, so a coordination of the full evaluation may thread a cage the screen does not consider. An
estimate ranks a proposal; it certifies nothing and discards nothing. Every proposal is still repaired, finalized,
deduplicated, evaluated completely and assessed by the code-check contract.

Section_Design.beam_rung_carries_moment (the uniform route's moment-based rung helper) is not used: it assumes one
tension layer at d = h - 3.5 in on a rectangular web (no flange, compression steel or mats), a fixed ratio
(BEAM_GROWTH_STEEL_RATIO, not the configured ceiling), phi 0.9 without a tension-control check, one moment for both
signs and no bar, lane, layer, minimum-steel or balance rule. Stacked rows put the tension centroid 5.5 to 8.0 in from
the face on o0005 (d = 22.0 to 24.5 in at h = 30 in), so it overstates the sections the search screens.

nodes.name: Genetic_Operators.py
nodes.summary: The six mutation operators of the genetic search (research contract six_operator_contract_reference_v1, 2026-10-30).
nodes.docstring_full:
The six mutation operators of the genetic search (research contract six_operator_contract_reference_v1, 2026-10-30).

  H1  strong-column / weak-beam: the next square size of each connected column tie; separately its family grade.
  H2  member strength: beam depth, beam width and beam-family grade alternatives; column size and column-family grade
      (for column capacity shear, no size step while the selected cage is at its minimum steel ratio, the
      longitudinal selection has settled and the probable-moment mechanism sets Ve under the column-own method: Ve
      then grows faster with the section than the 8 sqrt(f'c) b d limit. On the production route a cage that passes
      its P-M check is expected to have a mechanism-governed Ve; this is not established, so the record is read and
      the flag left unknown otherwise).
  H3  reinforcement space: bar room across the beam widens it, beam bars that do not thread grow the joint's core
      column, a slab-mat overlap needs its blocked dimension diagnosed first; a lane-limited beam strength shortfall
      (bar room, not strength) offers beam depth, beam width and the cores of the joints the beam frames into (only
      on a consistent joint topology, and only where it names such a joint), never a concrete grade; a
      threading-constrained strength shortfall (short of strength, with a stronger cage kept out by threading, v6)
      offers the beam's depth, width and grade, the blocking cores the record names among the joints the beam frames
      into (the next square size) and, where the selection's geometry-only look-ahead names one, the first larger core
      size whose lanes carry the stronger cage (lever column_lanes: a proposal for full evaluation, never a pass).
      Where the record separates the cores whose own cage blocks (blocking_core_cages), only those take column_up and
      column_lanes. A column transition that blocks (a band-boundary joint whose bar inventory closes the lanes) is
      named by both column groups; the first size of the column above, or of the core below, that opens that joint's
      own inventory is offered on that band (lever transition_lanes), only where the topology has a joint of the beam
      at which those two groups meet (v7, 2026-10-31 review). The same targeting (threading_levers) serves a failed
      threading row (beam_threading: the joint's core grows only where its own cage blocks; a transition-only blockage
      takes the band its joint look-ahead names, or is withheld when none is evidenced) and a lane-limited shortfall
      that carries the selection's threading fields (v8, 2026-10-31 follow-up review).
  H4  joint: joint shear compares core size and core-family grade; through-bar depth and hook embedment grow the core.
  H5  drift / stability: the SFRS columns of the implicated story and the beams (depth) of both floors that bound it,
      as separate alternatives.
  R1  random: a uniformly chosen mutable gene, then a uniformly chosen local neighbour (nearest lower/higher grade;
      the nondominated absolute dimension steps of a size).

A withheld lever (a rule that keeps a legal step back) is recorded with its rule, once per diagnostic and group,
only when the step exists (a larger square size); a lever without the evidence to aim it is recorded as withheld
for that reason: an inconsistent topology first, then a consistent one that names no joint the beam frames into.

Every guided proposal comes from a normalized diagnostic (Design.Genetic_Diagnostics) bound to the exact evaluated
parent and the run's evaluation basis; stale, unknown, invalid or dependency-incomplete evidence abstains with a
named reason, and a solver failure is never read as weakness. Each proposal requests one gene change. Size and
grade alternatives are separate proposals. The existing profile repair (Genetic_Search.DesignSpace.repair) then acts
on the whole profile, and ``finalize`` keeps the requested change apart from the changes repair induced: a repaired
genome equal to the parent is a no-op, a repair that removed or reversed the requested change is rejected. Nothing
here evaluates a design or grants acceptance. Crossover and adaptive operator weights are not part of this version.

v9 (2026-10-31, demand-sized jumps and severity-weighted selection; both are declared run policies, the earlier rules
remain as local_frontier_v1 and uniform_operator_v1):

  Demand-sized beam-flexure jumps (ctx["guided_policy"]["beam_jump"] == demand_sized_v1). A beam flexural shortfall
      (beam_flexure, beam_lane_limited_strength, beam_threading_constrained_strength) keeps its local steps and may add,
      per lever (depth, width, grade_up; the levers its route already offers), the one farther option the parent's
      screen shortlisted (Design.Genetic_Jumps: the smallest option estimated to reach the target DCR on the frozen
      parent demand, or a useful partial improvement when none is). The screen is read only when bound to this parent
      and basis and to the gene's current allele; otherwise, or when it shortlisted nothing, the route records why
      (route["jumps"]). A jump is one requested gene with the lever's own direction; its origin carries the estimate,
      which ranks the proposal and never certifies it.
  Severity-weighted guided selection (choose_guided with policy severity_weighted_v1). The routes that proposed are
      grouped by an actionable failure key (failure_key: the design tie, i.e. the size gene, of the member group of a
      strength, capacity-shear or bar-room failure; the beam's tie and the joint core of a threading failure; the joint
      core of a joint or strong-column failure; the column band of a story drift or stability failure). Each key takes
      the largest severity of its diagnostics (severity = max(0, u - 1), u = demand / capacity for "<=" checks and
      required / provided for ">=" checks, from the authenticated diagnostic; a check without a defensible ratio takes
      the declared categorical weight, and an unbounded one, no available clearance or capacity, the weight at the cap)
      and the weight selection_weight: floor + (1 - floor) min(severity, cap) / cap. Each distinct proposal is drawn
      with probability proportional to its share, the largest over the keys that offer it of the key's weight divided
      by the key's number of distinct proposals. So repeated rows, extra catalog alternatives and a proposal offered
      by two operators or two keys add no weight, a key that shares no proposal is drawn in proportion to its weight,
      and every eligible key keeps at least the floor. Only routes that proposed carry weight: unknown, stale, invalid
      or abstaining evidence acquires none. The weights follow the current violations, not learned operator
      performance; the random-exploration probability, parent selection and survival are unchanged.

v10 (2026-11-01, severity plus demand-sized preference; a third declared selection policy, the earlier two remain):

  severity_preferred_jumps_v1 (choose_guided). Under severity_weighted_v1 a failure's weight is spread evenly over its
      proposed fixes, so a screened demand-sized change and a small local step of the same failure are equally likely
      whatever their estimates. This policy changes the allocation between failure families and between fixes: it is
      not severity-only selection. Each guided draw is a mixture:
        with probability preferred_share (default 0.80) when the preferred pool is not empty, the preferred branch;
        otherwise, and with probability 1 - preferred_share, the severity_weighted_v1 draw over every eligible proposal.
      The guided probability itself (and so the R1 branch) is unchanged. The preferred pool holds the distinct
      proposals that the parent's demand-sized screen shortlisted (an origin with step demand_sized, authenticated by
      route: bound to this parent, basis and allele; a local origin of the same genome does not remove it) for a
      failure key whose utilization (its largest authenticated ratio) is at least severe_utilization (default 1.25).
      Each candidate is scored against its own beam unit: b, the unit's baseline estimate, and e, the unit's estimate
      under the change (``matched``; never another band's estimate), with target t and gain floor g (the jump policy's
      target DCR and min_gain):
        excluded when b <= t (no deficit in the screen); when e needs a cage that does not thread the frozen column
        cages (the unit's estimate pool is not "threading": a beam-only change does not reach anything there, the
        column clearance and coordination proposals stay in the normal branch); when b - e < g or b - e <= 0 (a
        negligible improvement); or when e <= t while a smaller option the route also proposes reaches the unit's
        target (larger_than_unit_target: the smaller one carries the preference);
        f = 1 when e <= t (estimated to reach the target), otherwise f = (b - e) / (b - t), the fraction of the unit's
        deficit closed (comparable across demand levels). The screen shortlists a gene's smallest option reaching the
        target, and a concrete family's follows its worst unit; so the screen also gives each unit's own smallest
        option reaching the target with a threading cage (unit_targets). Whatever the gene's own shortlist (also none,
        or another lever's move), when the route already proposes that option (a local step of a jump lever whose
        direction contains it) the route annotates it as that unit's demand-sized target. No proposal is added, so
        every policy draws over the same genomes; the annotation is evidence in the logs under every policy, counted
        apart (jump_routes.unit_target, jump_unit_target_steps_drawn). unit_smallest_confirmed records that the
        candidate is the unit's smallest target option and that unit was priced at every smaller legal option.
      A key K with weight w_K (selection_weight) and candidates C_K gives candidate p the score
        s(p, K) = w_K * f*_K * f(p, K) / sum over q in C_K of f(q, K),   f*_K = max over C_K of f,
      so a key's preferred mass is its weight times its best usefulness, split by usefulness (more alternatives add
      none). A candidate offered for several keys takes its largest score (never a sum; the first key in key order on
      a tie). P_preferred(p) = s(p) / sum of s. The final probability of a proposal is
        P(p) = a * P_preferred(p) + (1 - a) * P_normal(p),   a = preferred_share if the pool is not empty, else 0.
      Two rng.random() per guided draw (the branch, then the proposal over sorted genomes), so a seed reproduces the
      draws. A candidate already drawn for this parent in either branch (``exhausted``; the controller keeps them in its
      checkpoint) is excluded, so repair no-ops, duplicates and cache hits are not drawn again from it; an
      empty pool falls back to the normal branch with the reason (no_screened_candidate, no_eligible_severe_candidate,
      preferred_pool_exhausted). Only beam-flexure screens have an estimator: drift, column P-M, joint shear and the
      other checks keep their routes and their severity weighting in the normal branch, and so do the column clearance
      and coordination proposals of a threading-constrained beam (a beam-only change whose target stays unmet says so).
      The preferred_share and severe_utilization defaults are experimental search parameters, not code thresholds.

nodes.name: Genetic_Population.py
nodes.summary: Population selection and accepted-design retention of the genetic search (2026-10-30).
nodes.docstring_full:
Population selection and accepted-design retention of the genetic search (2026-10-30).

Selection policy SELECTION_POLICY (research policy population_archive_semantics_v1, adapted to the production
code-check contract), an explicit starting option, not a tuned or validated rule:

  eligibility   a search parent is a valid, numerically complete record that is code-accepted or has at least one
                known failure. A record without an observed failure but with missing evidence goes to the evidence
                queue; a stopped, erroring or numerically incomplete one to the analysis-recovery queue; an invalid
                one is never a parent. Missing evidence is never a zero violation.
  tiers         code-accepted (0), complete with known failures (1), unresolved with known failures (2).
  coverage      within the unresolved tier, more known required checks is preferred only between designs with the
                same expected inventory (inventory_id); different inventories are never compared on coverage.
  progress      (maximum known exceedance, mean of the per-family maximum known exceedances), the family being the
                contract family and check id (PROGRESS_FAMILY_RULE). Compared only between designs of the same tier
                whose comparison signature is equal: same inventory, same known-check mask and the same basis (clause,
                comparison, units, branch) of every known check. Code-accepted designs never dominate one another.
  fronts        nondominated sorting under that (acyclic) dominance; a front larger than the open slots is thinned
                by fixed-domain diversity: a seeded anchor, then greedy maximum-minimum distance over the declared
                section and grade ranges (each size gene the mean of its width and depth distances, each grade gene
                its grade distance), never rescaled to the observed population.
  witnesses     every selected design keeps its local regressions against the other candidates: worsened violations,
                worsened utilizations (passing checks included), evidence lost, checks whose basis or applicability
                changed. Survival is not acceptance and not an engineering improvement.
  quarantine    a realized design observed with contradictory evidence anywhere in the history (``history``) is no
                parent and is listed in the queues (v2: v1 looked only at the candidates passed in).

The archive views are recomputed from the full evaluation history and never delete it: every distinct code-accepted
realized design (keyed by case, evaluation basis and realized identity, material dominance notwithstanding), a
bounded diversity view of that registry, the evidence queue grouped by missing source (each realized design counted
once, quarantined ones left to the quarantine view), the analysis-recovery queue, the unroutable failures (failing
rows the router's first gates keep from every operator: evidence that did not authenticate, no declared mutation
reason, incomplete trigger dependencies; later abstentions such as no legal move are counted in the run's
abstentions instead), quarantined identities with contradictory observations and descriptor collisions. Qualification and
nonlinear statuses are carried unchanged.

nodes.name: Genetic_Search.py
nodes.summary: Experimental grouped genetic search with failure-guided mutation.
nodes.docstring_full:
Experimental grouped genetic search with failure-guided mutation.

One fixed grouping/layout and longitudinal grade per run. Genes are declared
section rungs (one per tie) and concrete grades (one per family). Reinforcement
is reselected by the existing evaluator from a reproducible seed cage.

Every evaluation passes the code-check contract before it is ranked or archived
(Design.Code_Check_Contract.assess_evaluation, 2026-10-30): the record's schema,
explicit completion flags, the seed identity captured before evaluation, the
final state and its identity, and the code-check rows, recomputed against an
inventory derived from the final design itself. Only an "accepted" candidate
(the complete scoped code check passed, the evaluation completed, the
objectives available) enters the archive; "check_failed", "unresolved" and
"invalid" candidates keep their known failures as fields and as secondary
fitness keys, never as a pass. Review dependencies are listed, not asserted.
Nothing here is a design qualification: the saved record's qualification
(Design.Grouped_Record) remains the gate before any analysis.

No production runner imports this module. Evaluation remains serial because
OpenSees and Structure_Parameters have process-global state.

nodes.name: Gravity_Frame_Members.py
nodes.summary: Members not designated as part of the seismic-force-resisting system: ACI 318-19 18.14 (2026-10-16).
nodes.docstring_full:
Members not designated as part of the seismic-force-resisting system: ACI 318-19 18.14 (2026-10-16).

Under the perimeter-frame basis (user decision 2026-10-16) the special moment frames are the four perimeter
frames and every interior beam and column is a gravity member: designed for the gravity combinations of 5.3
and detailed for compatibility with the design displacement delta_u (18.14.2.1, 18.14.3.1). The branch of
18.14.3 a member falls in depends on the moments and shears induced in it at delta_u:

* 18.14.3.2, induced effects within the design strengths (Mu <= phi Mn and Vu <= phi Vn):
  (a) beams: 18.6.3.1 longitudinal limits; transverse reinforcement per 25.7 over the whole length at not
      more than d/2; hoops per 18.7.5.2 at not more than the lesser of 6 db and 6 in where Pu > Ag f'c / 10;
  (b) columns: 18.7.4.1 (rho 1 to 6 percent) and 18.7.6 (design shear); hoops per 25.7.4 over the full length
      at not more than the lesser of 6 db and 6 in; the 18.7.5.2(a) to (e) configuration over l0 (18.7.5.1);
  (c) columns with Pu > 0.35 Po also provide half the greater of Table 18.7.5.4 (a) and (b) over l0;
  (d) joints per Chapter 15.
* 18.14.3.3, induced effects above phi Mn or phi Vn, or not calculated:
  (a) materials and splices per 18.2.5 to 18.2.8; (b) beams per 18.14.3.2(a) and 18.6.5 (capacity shear);
  (c) columns per 18.7.4, 18.7.5 and 18.7.6, 18.7.4.3 excepted; (d) joints per the intermediate-frame joint
      shear rule (318-25 18.4.4.1).

The text was read from the ACI 318-25 book on 2026-10-16; the record's declared edition stays 318-19, whose
18.14.3 says the same in substance. 18.14.1.1 limits the section to SDC D, E and F; the research population
applies it to its SDC C frames as well, as a declared design-basis choice, so one rule covers the dataset.
